question: What protective claim is made about the body of one who has practiced, even if bitten by great serpents?
premises: A person may be bitten by great serpents.
Poison is the agent in such a bite.
For one in the state produced by this practice, poison does not enter the body.
inference: Even if bitten by great serpents, poison does not enter the body of one who has attained this state.
uncertainties: State attained is presupposed from verses 122-123
plain_english: Poison does not enter the body, even if one has been bitten by great serpents.
